161	
162	**PC-5. Aim and the beam.** *Sources.* Mouse: raw aim = direction from the **aim origin** `AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos_curr) + (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y)` (a fixed reference chest height, independent of facing, sheet and animation row; default `AIM_ORIGIN_Y` = −35) to the cursor's **look-ahead-free world point** `cursor_aim_world = f_q + (cursor_vp − picture_centre) / k_eff`, where `f_q` is the pipeline's **published** follow pose **before** look-ahead, the inner-box clamp and jolt (pipeline D.6's `f`, floored to the camera quantum; pipeline D.14b publishes it every frame), `cursor_vp` the cursor in **physical window px** relative to the world picture's origin, `picture_centre = (L_w, L_h) · k_z / 2` in the same unit and `k_eff = k_z` the physical px per base px (the unit is the pipeline's D.14b `cursor_px`; whether `Viewport.get_mouse_position()` already returns window px or stretched base units under the `canvas_items` stretch is **[UNV]** — the engine reference does not settle it — so the Adapter takes the cursor through the inverse of the window's final transform, and the pipeline's in-engine acceptance criterion in "Camera follow, look-ahead, cuts" gates the aim story); inside `AIM_MOUSE_DEADZONE_PX` = 8 base px of the aim origin the aim holds, **measured in picture space with the camera settled** (the near-body fixtures in Acceptance Criteria are authored that way; while the follow lag is non-zero the cursor-to-origin distance carries the lag term below). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R4: the Controller's form is canonical and the pipeline publishes `f_q`, a contract, no longer a request; the review's alternative of anchoring on the avatar `p = floor(pos_curr)` was not adopted, see the trade-off below)* **Why not C11's `cursor_world`:** C11 maps through `pose_q`, which includes the look-ahead `L`, and `L` is a function of this very aim; the loop (aim moves camera, camera moves the world point under a still cursor, which moves aim) would slew the beam towards a near cursor and keep it drifting after the mouse stops, with no cursor drawn to explain it. Measuring against `f_q` breaks the loop: `f_q` depends on the avatar's motion only, so with the avatar still a still cursor gives a constant `aim_q` while the look-ahead settles, and the beam still goes where the hidden cursor is *relative to the avatar*. The Adapter reads exactly two presentation values from the pipeline for this: `f_q` (published, pipeline D.14b) and the screen→picture mapping (`picture_centre`, `k_eff`); it reads no sim block for it beyond `body.state.pos_curr`. **Recorded trade-off** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R4)*: the aim is `cursor_aim_world − AIM_ORIGIN = (f_q − floor(pos_curr)) + cursor_off − (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y)`, so it is a function of the cursor, the follow lag `f_q − pos` and `k_eff`. With the avatar still the lag is zero and a still mouse gives a constant aim whatever the look-ahead does; **when a run starts or stops, `S = f_q − floor(pos_curr)` changes by at most 36 px at `v_run` (24 at walk): the lag part ≤ 32.4 px (the dt→0 bound; 30.9 px at 60 fps), the tick phase ≤ 3 px, floor 1 px (pipeline D.6, D.14b; D.7 variable `f_q`), and a still mouse turns the beam by the geometry of that shift** (about 31°, `atan(36/60)`, for a cursor 60 px from the avatar at full shift; about 10°, `atan(36/200)`, at 200 px), with no input from the player *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. This is accepted because the reference the hidden cursor is read against is the *picture* (the camera's follow pose), which is also what the player sees move; the review's alternative of anchoring on the avatar position would hold the beam rigid against the hand but put the hidden-cursor reference up to 104 px (32.4 px of lag plus the 72 px look-ahead) off the drawn avatar. Neither form puts the reference on the drawn avatar; the cost of the chosen form is bounded and is measured by the target-acquisition item of the motion-integrity spike (Game Feel, "Target acquisition protocol"), with pre-recorded fallbacks. Pillar 1's "the beam is your hand" is protected where it matters most: the beam never moves when the avatar is still, and its origin and shape are untouched. The beam is **drawn** from the real `CHEST_POINT` (PC-5 below); only the *measurement* uses the fixed reference, so a facing flip (the chest point moves up to 4 px horizontally, more vertically across rows) can never move the aim, and the sheet/flip/beam limit cycle with a near cursor cannot occur. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: loop break and facing-independent aim origin; the 2026-10-26 user decision "mouse aim is the direction from the floored chest point to the cursor" is honoured as the **reference chest** — a presentation-neutral measurement point that does not change what the player sees or does; the beam origin is still the true chest point. Confirmed 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): D10, this reading of the decision is accepted: a fixed reference chest `AIM_ORIGIN` measures the aim, the beam is drawn from the true chest point. Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* Gamepad right stick: **radial dead-zone `AIM_DEADZONE` = 0.20 (0.10–0.35), scaled-radial, outer `AIM_OUTER` = 0.90, curve exponent `AIM_CURVE` = 1.0; no magnetism, no snap, no slow-down near targets, no input-side smoothing by default**. Keyboard: the arrow keys and `aim_hold` give octant-centre aim (PC-2). **Released-stick behaviour is one setting with three states, `aim_release_mode` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: replaces the binary `aim_follows_movement` knob; folds amendment (9))*:**
163	
164	| `aim_release_mode` | A released stick (aim-idle) … | Used by |
165	|---|---|---|
166	| `FOLLOW_MOVE_WHEN_RELEASED` | slews towards the movement octant centre at `AIM_FOLLOW_SLEW` (default 64 units/tick = 5.6°/tick, so a 180° swing takes 32 ticks; the lamp never whips and never stays stuck on the last door); holds when standing still; any right-stick deflection takes over at once | **the default** *(Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): D8, Open Question 21. Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
167	| `HOLD` | holds the last aim forever; until the **first** right-stick deflection of the session the aim follows the movement octant centre (amendment (9): so a pad player who never aims is not stuck pointing south) | an option in Settings (the previously decided amendment (9), no longer the default; it brings back the lamp stuck on a door once the player has aimed) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
168	| `FOLLOW_ALWAYS` | the stick is never live; `aim_angle` = movement octant centre on every octant change (one `set_aim` per change); standing still holds; mouse motion takes over | the one-handed preset |
169	
170	In all three modes a deflected stick is absolute-direction aim and wins immediately; `live` is false whenever the stick is released or in `FOLLOW_ALWAYS`. *Two consumers.* The **raw aim** is read locally by the Avatar Presenter (the local beam's `Light2D` rotation, continuous, in the same frame — lights may rotate off-grid, PR-4 rule 5) and by the camera look-ahead (C4, regardless of lit state); the look-ahead consumes the *angle* of the raw aim measured against `f_q`, so it feeds on a quantity it cannot move *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, **weighted toward the movement direction while running** by the pipeline's own D.7 formula (D6 option B: `w = LOOKAHEAD_RUN_WEIGHT · smoothstep(V_WALK, V_RUN, |v|)`, default 0.50, owned and tuned by the pipeline; D.7b cites it and defines nothing of its own, so walking, standing, carrying and channelling keep the pure aim look-ahead and the boarding-rhythm sweep is unchanged) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings; re-review, general rule G1: the Controller-side formula and knob `RUN_LOOKAHEAD_MOVE_WEIGHT` are withdrawn)*. The **committed aim** (`aim_angle`, 1/4096 turn, ≤ 1 tick late, ≥ 1/128-turn send threshold) is what Emitter State orients the beam emitter by for the exposure query, what Interaction's focus weighting uses, what facing derives from, and what co-op replicates. A ≤ 2.8° / ≤ 1-tick divergence between the drawn and simulated cone is accepted; the identity channel (Pillar 1) is shape and colour, which come from the replicated loadout, never from aim.
171	
172	*Cursor warp and source handover (one Adapter rule, presentation-local).* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the 35 px origin offset does not scale with `k`, so a zoom step turned the beam under a still mouse, and the first mouse movement after stick use snapped the beam to a stale cursor position; the earlier acceptance criteria allowed both.)* The OS cursor is hidden and confined in `gameplay`, so the Adapter may reposition it without the player seeing a pointer move. **(i) Zoom edge:** on a `zoom_in` / `zoom_out` step (the pipeline's `RESCALING` frame) the Adapter warps the hidden cursor to `picture_centre + cursor_off_old × k_eff_new`, keeping `cursor_off` (base px) and therefore `aim_q` unchanged within ±1 unit; if the target position falls outside the window the warp clamps and the aim may differ (the confinement rectangle is the window, Edge Cases). **(ii) Handover to the mouse:** while the aim source is STICK or KEYS the mouse takes over only after `AIM_MOUSE_TAKEOVER_PX` (default 6 physical window px, **[PLACEHOLDER — derive at spike]**, range 2–16) of accumulated cursor travel, so a nudged desk does not hijack the lamp; at takeover the Adapter first warps the cursor to the point whose direction from `AIM_ORIGIN` is the current raw aim and whose radius is `max(last |r|, AIM_WARP_RADIUS_PX)` (default 48 base px, **[PLACEHOLDER]**, range 16–96), so the first mouse sample holds the aim it found instead of jumping to a stale position. **(iii) `aim_source` ∈ {AUTO, MOUSE, STICK, KEYS}:** `AUTO` (default) follows the last aim axis, with (ii) applied on a handover to the mouse; `MOUSE`, `STICK` or `KEYS` force one source and ignore the others (no handover, no warp on the forced source; the mouse stays warped only for (i)). A warp is Adapter-local presentation: it submits nothing, writes no block and reveals no sim state.
173	
174	*Beam shapes are a loadout, not an input.* The four shapes (wide, narrow, split, fan — art bible 3.2, 8.3) are a per-player Suit & Equipment fact; there is no "change shape" action. `beam_toggle` submits **`toggle_beam`** (owner: Emitter State; actor = the seat's beam emitter ID). The beam is an emitter like any other for Attention, which is what makes "go dark" a strategy.
175	
176	*Acknowledgement vs the anchor.* The beam is a human-channel anchor that may never lie. If the local light lit on the press and the sim then rejected (`CHARGE_EMPTY`), the beam would flicker once on the one object that may not. Rule: **the toggle's sound and the hand's switch animation pre-play immediately; the light itself changes only on committed state** (≤ 17 ms later, imperceptible against a 3-screen-px cone edge). The Avatar Presenter never predicts beam state. **Pose and value split (LO-2):** the Presenter publishes the local beam pose — position and rotation only — and 2D Lighting & Occlusion writes the value members (`enabled`, `energy`, `texture`, `color`) from `emitter.state`; the Presenter's pose write precedes Lighting's apply in the render callback. **Toggle rate limit (accessibility, WCAG 2.3.1):** the Adapter submits no `toggle_beam` within `BEAM_TOGGLE_MIN_INTERVAL_TICKS` = 12 ticks of its previous submitted `toggle_beam`; a press inside the window is dropped (no pre-play, no click, nothing submitted), so input can flip the beam at most five times (2.5 flashes) per second, inside the WCAG 2.3.1 limit of three with a margin (the earlier 10 ticks allowed exactly three flashes per second, at the limit with none) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: 10 → 12; the value also stops the Adapter permitting a toggle that Emitter State's own 12-tick switch cooldown would answer `TOO_SOON`)*. The 12-tick floor also covers Suit's six-tick (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`) sampled-drain window (SE-35). A sim-side guard in `toggle_beam.validate` is Emitter State's to add (Open Questions). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from 2d-lighting-and-occlusion, emitter-state-and-light-exposure-query, suit-and-equipment)*
177	
178	*Chest point (beam origin) and hand point (tool grip).* The beam's origin is `floor(interp_pos) + CHEST_POINT[facing][animation]`, mirrored as `(−x, y)` for the three mirrored facings, using the same floored position as the sprite (PR-4 rule 2) so light origin and sprite never disagree; the table is per facing **and per animation** (run lean, carry and stagger frames move it slightly), and art keeps `|x| ≤ 2 px` so a mirror barely moves the light (registry `chest_point`; user decision 2026-10-26 — chest-mounted, hands-free lamp). `HAND_POINT[facing][animation]` is the separate tool-grip anchor and carries no light. The Controller Sim publishes both points in its read view so that when the Perception Filter substitutes a horror rig (class c, art bible 5.0) the beam still originates at the *true* chest point. *(Amended 2026-10-26 — consistency check)*
179	
180	**PC-6. One focus model, interaction reach, lit-only actions, hold-to-confirm.** *Reach* is a sector from the foot origin: `REACH_PX` = 72 base px (1.5 tiles — the adjacent ring including diagonals at 68 px), half-angle `REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG` = 70° about the **facing**. Objects behind the player are never candidates. *Focus — the same model on every device:* among interactables that are in reach, in the arc and **lit** (Emitter State's exposure query above the technical-artist's threshold), the focused one minimises `score = d / REACH_PX + FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT × θ / REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG`, with `θ` the angle between the object's direction from the foot origin and the **ground-projected aim** (mouse: the direction from the foot origin to `cursor_aim_world`, PC-5; stick and keys: the committed aim, a direction only) and `FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT` = 1.0 (0.5–2.0), `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` = 0.10 (D.9) — **aim-weighted proximity** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: measuring θ from the chest-height aim origin made a floor object the player points straight at read 30° off; the focus score is Adapter-side presentation, so the ground projection changes no sim value, and `in_reach` is untouched)*; the mouse has no separate pick-under-cursor path (the cursor moves the aim, and aim weights the score, so the model is one). Exactly one object is focused; the HUD draws its prompt (`E · Cut`) only when lit (art bible 7.0), at `world_to_hud(target)`; an off-screen object has no prompt (C9). **Self-target rule** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP, blocker PC-6 focus model)*: the candidate set has one fallback member, the actor's own suit (object class `ACTOR_SELF`). It is nominated if and only if (i) Suit's `tool_in_hand(player_id)` (the actor's own hand rail, SE-40, read like `carried_instance`) names a tool for which Interaction's declaration data has an `ACTOR_SELF` row (today `tool_welder`, the self-patch of IA-17; matched on the exact tool only, IA-5 tier (1), no `NEEDS_TOOL` fallback), (ii) `carry_ref == none` and `loco_state ∉ {DOWNED, DEAD, IN_POD}`, and (iii) the world candidate set (in reach, in arc, lit) is empty. It is the focus only while (iii) holds: any world candidate displaces it on the frame that candidate appears, and `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` never holds the self-target against a world candidate. Its score is `SELF_FOCUS_SCORE = 2 + FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT × 180 / REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG + FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` (D.9), load-computed and not a knob (4.67 at defaults), so it is above every world score. The Adapter submits `begin_patch {target_ref = own PlayerId}`, mode `CHANNEL`, under the PC-7 hold policy. No lit or reach test applies (the row is `act_gate`-exempt, IA-6), and the Controller never reads `integrity_bp` or any suit reading to decide that the self-target exists: a healthy suit is Interaction's `NOTHING_TO_REPAIR` outcome (IA-17), so there is no oracle. An unlit object, a phantom and an empty floor all leave the world set empty and give the identical self-target (Pillar 4). `focus_view.self_target` is true (Interaction IA-41) and the HUD draws the plate at the chest keep-out (HS-37, HS-39); the lit rule is not applied to it. Consequence, accepted: with the welder in hand and any lit candidate in reach and arc, the world candidate wins; the player turns the facing away from it (mouse: aim away; pad: move or aim away) to reach the self-prompt. **The Adapter never chooses the verb**: `interact` is one button, and **Interaction declares, per focused object and equipped tool, the command type and its mode** ∈ {`TAP`, `HOLD_CONFIRM`, `CHANNEL`}; the Adapter applies the matching policy over the same commands. **Decision (art bible 7.0 leaves it to the game-designer): an action is possible only on a lit object.** Interaction's `validate` calls the exposure query the prompt uses, so the prompt never lies by omission. *Rationale:* "what you light, you can read" must also be "what you light, you can touch", or working in the dark becomes a free Attention dodge and "go dark" degenerates into the dominant strategy; light has to cost Attention for darkness to be a trade. Exceptions are Interaction's `act_gate` exempt rows (registry `act_gate`): `drop` of the carried module, `toggle_beam`, the inspect card of an already-lit instrument, `throw_glowstick` and, by the resolution below, every `ACTOR_SELF` verb. **Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling G1 with the re-review's recommendation (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): option (a), `ACTOR_SELF` verbs are an `act_gate` exempt row (Open Question 16).** The self-patch (`begin_patch` on object class `ACTOR_SELF`, Interaction IA-17) is the only MVP way to repair the suit (Suit SE-22). As Interaction, Emitter State and the registry stood it could never pass the lit check: Emitter State EM-21 adds the owner's own beam to the owner's `lux_pm` only and states it "is not added to the owner's `act_lux_pm`" (the player is never the target of their own verb), the `lit` flag is computed from `act_lux_pm`, and Interaction listed `NOT_LIT` for `begin_patch`, so a player alone with the lamp on got `NOT_LIT`. "What you light, you can touch" was never meant to read "you cannot patch your own suit in the dark"; read that way the Pillar 3 "go dark" lever would be a trap. So `ACTOR_SELF` verbs join the exempt rows beside `drop`, `toggle_beam`, the inspect card and `throw_glowstick`; EM-21's "never the target of your own verb" stays intact everywhere else. The "known defect" wording is withdrawn. Consequences stated here so the siblings can conform: the lamp-off result is `Applied` (patching yourself in the dark is legal), and the mid-channel unlit re-check of PC-7 (v) skips a channel whose target class is `ACTOR_SELF`, because there is no lit object to lose. **Siblings conformed 2026-10-28 (delegated G6):** Interaction IA-6 / D.2 / IA-7 / IA-14 / IA-17 and the registry `act_gate` (owner Interaction) exempt the `ACTOR_SELF` self-patch as an actor verb, and Emitter State EM-21 is unchanged and notes why. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review, delegated ruling G1)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6; conformance)* Web Map & Transit's request to exempt `pod_hop` from the lit conjunct (ASK-I2) is Interaction's to accept in `act_gate`; `in_reach` (D.9) keeps its lit conjunct. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from web-map-and-transit)* *Hold-to-confirm* (`HOLD_CONFIRM` mode — destructive verbs, HR-14): a **local** hold of `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` = 0.8 s (0.6–1.2) in render time, drawn on the art bible 7.3 **linear bar — never a ring** (routed correction to the kernel's "progress ring" wording); **release drains the bar at 2×**; on completion one command is submitted; the sim never sees a partial hold. Option: **tap-to-confirm** — two taps, arm then confirm, within `CONFIRM_TAP_WINDOW` = 3 s. No QTEs anywhere. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; D.10 has the arithmetic.)* **Hardening:** (i) each frame adds at most `CONFIRM_DT_MAX_S` = 0.05 s to the bar, so a single 1 s hitch cannot confirm a destructive cut; (ii) the target is **latched** while the bar is above zero: a focus change during a hold neither transfers nor completes the bar, it drains at 2× on the latched target and the new focus starts from zero after release; (iii) modes are exclusive per declaration (IA-8): a `HOLD_CONFIRM` verb submits one `TAP`-class command on completion and never a `begin_*`; if a future verb needs confirm-then-work, Interaction declares it as a `CHANNEL` with a confirm step, the completed bar submits `begin_<verb>`, the plate resets to zero and the HUD re-fills it from the channel's committed progress, and the held `interact` then sustains the channel in hold mode (the "release before re-arm" rule belongs to the confirm bar only); (iv) the tap-window timer is frozen while the kernel is `PAUSED` and disarms on context change.
181	
182	**PC-7. Channels (cut / weld / patch).** `interact` on an object whose declared mode is `CHANNEL` → the Adapter submits `begin_<verb> {target}` (`coalesce = NONE`; owner Interaction, Assembly behind it for weld/cut). The owner's `validate` requires: lit and in reach, except an `ACTOR_SELF` channel (no lit or reach test, PC-6) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6; conformance)*, **`controller.state.intent_octant == NONE`**, not carrying, not staggered/downed. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `intent_octant` and `intent_run` are written by the `set_move_intent` `apply` handler in P2; `octant` is the value `controller.step` publishes in P3 and the channel owners' hooks read. Validation that read `octant` saw last tick's value, so releasing W and pressing E in one frame was rejected, and pressing W and E together was accepted and then aborted silently. With the split the first applies and the second is rejected at once with reason `MOVING` (immediate class, "no" cue; proposed to Interaction, today folded into `BUSY` — Open Question 25). Both rely on the Adapter submitting intents before commands in a frame (PC-2).)* **Progress is sim state in `interaction.state`** (with `owner_system` ASSEMBLY for weld and section cut), accrued per tick by Interaction's hook; the owner's `apply` records `channel_ref`, `channel_face` and `channel_body` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6; INTERNAL fix)* through the Controller's `set_channel_ref(actor, owner_system, channel_id, face_octant)` mutator (PC-1 b) and the Controller holds facing at `channel_face` (PC-4 rule 2); `loco_state` becomes `CHANNELLING` in that tick's `controller.step` by the precedence function of States and Transitions *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from modular-ship-assembly, interaction-system)* **Hold is the default; a toggle option exists; both are Adapter policy over the same two commands.** *Interrupts:* (i) **release** (hold mode) or a second press / `cancel` (toggle mode) → `cancel_channel`; (ii) **movement** — `controller.step` itself clears `channel_ref` and `channel_face` in the tick an applied intent has `octant ≠ NONE` (step 3 of the `controller.step` order, so the move wins on that same tick and the first movement step is not lost), and the owner's hook, declared `after: controller.step`, reads `controller.state.octant` and aborts (sim-side, so identical in `MIRROR`; the 8-way dead-zone already filters stick drift) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; (iii) **stagger / downed** — the Controller Sim clears `channel_ref`; (iv) **target invalidated** (power drops mid-cut, the section detaches) — the owner aborts and reports through state change, never through the command result (CR-5); (v) **unlit** — the owner re-checks the target's `lit` every `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS` (6, Interaction IA-7) and aborts `UNLIT` (not for a channel whose target class is `ACTOR_SELF`: that verb is `act_gate`-exempt, PC-6, Open Question 16 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*); **proposed grace** (accessibility; Interaction's to adopt, Open Question 25): `LIT_ABORT_GRACE_TICKS` = 30 (0–60, extendable by an accessibility setting) is a counter to which each consecutive dark check adds `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS` (so 30 = five consecutive dark checks) and a lit check resets, so tremor, stick drift or sliding off a narrow beam edge no longer aborts a 360-tick weld while a lamp that is switched off still aborts within half a second *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; (vi) a body transfer (step 1's body edge: the stamped `channel_body` no longer equals `body_of_actor`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6; INTERNAL fix)*, a restore (snapshot normalisation), and entry to `chart_table` or `chat` (Contexts, PC-2). The player keeps control of the body at all times: a channel never locks movement, movement cancels the channel. *Rationale:* Dread Before Chaos needs "I can leave now" to be true in every state. **Pause:** the tick stops, progress freezes; on resume the hold survives if the button is still down (PC-2 resync). Whether partial progress persists on the target after an abort is **Interaction's rule** (IA-16). Channel feedback (sounds → audio-director): *start* (pre-play: hand animation + tool start sound + bar appears), *confirmed* (bar begins filling from committed state), *progress* (work loop + tool loop sound), *cancel* (release: bar drains at 2×, tool stops), *abort* (owner-driven: bar snaps empty, a distinct interrupted cue), *completion* (bar fills, completion cue, work loop ends), *rejection* (immediate class: ack withdrawn within a frame, a dull "no" cue); a free-lie-detector channel is never a rejection — it is identical to *confirmed* until it resolves to its `PRECONDITION` outcome (KRN:96). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from interaction-system)* "Stopped", "interrupted" and "nothing happened" are three different sounds.
183	
184	**PC-8. Carrying.** `pickup` (Interaction) sets `controller.state.carry_ref` through `set_carry_ref`; `carry_drop` → `drop` clears it through `clear_carry_ref` (PC-1 b; Assembly also calls `clear_carry_ref` on an install). No trigger is needed, so no mutator (`set_carry_ref`, `clear_carry_ref`, an install, a `pickup`, a `drop`) can leave the class inconsistent, and the diagnostics' "invalid pair" rule applies only to pairs with an endpoint outside the class. The class members may all enter `STAGGERED`, `DOWNED` and `IN_POD`. `CHANNELLING` is not a trigger-driven transition at all: it is **derived** from `channel_ref` by the precedence function in the step order below, so the legal same-frame release-W/press-E case (`set_move_intent {NONE}` applies, then `begin_*` validates against `intent_octant == NONE` and applies) yields `CHANNELLING` on that tick, and the per-tick class function can never overwrite it on the next. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier "`IDLE` alone enters `CHANNELLING`" made that case an invalid pair, and the class function would have overwritten `CHANNELLING` on the next tick.)*

258	**`controller.step` order (normative).** One run per controlled actor per tick (divisor 1, `after: suit.vitals`, P3), in exactly this order *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: new; the sub-rules in PC-4, PC-7, PC-9, D.4, D.5, D.8 and D.14 are the detail of these steps)*:
259	
260	1. **Cap edge and body edge.** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6; INTERNAL fix: body edge added)* Read `locomotion_cap` and compare it with the stored `cap_seen` (PC-9). A falling edge `FULL → WALK_ONLY` in any state except `DOWNED`, `DEAD` and `IN_POD` sets `stagger_end_tick := T + STAGGER_TICKS` (a stagger already running keeps its timer; a `SYSTEM` `stagger` command's `apply` has already set it in P2, with the same rule) and clears `channel_ref` and `channel_face`. Cap `NONE` outside `DEAD` sets, once, `T_downed := T` and `death_tick := T + DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS`, clears `channel_ref` and `channel_face`, and drops the carried module at the foot origin (kept while the body is the pod, D60). A cap rising from `NONE` clears `T_downed` and `death_tick`. **Body edge:** read `body_of_actor(actor)` (a pure Body read; a BM3 weld for an actor on the absorbed body, a BM4 detach and a BM5 pod hop, either direction, apply in P2 and `controller.step` runs in P3 of the same tick, so the read is current). If `channel_ref` is set and `channel_body` differs from `body_of_actor(actor)`, clear `channel_ref`, `channel_face` and `channel_body` now, in every state and before step 4, so `IN_POD` never sits above a stale ref and the ref cannot resurface as `CHANNELLING` when the actor leaves the pod; `octant`, `carry_ref` and `facing` are kept. A transfer that leaves the actor's body unchanged (a weld, for an actor on the host body, BDY-22) clears nothing. The `BODY_TRANSFER` event is a P5 notification and is never the trigger. Step numbering is unchanged, so every "steps 1 and 3" citation stays valid; an Interaction channel that completes (IA-14 row 9) clears its own ref before a weld applies (MSA E-56), so the two never conflict. Last, `cap_seen := cap`, in every state.
261	2. **Timers.** `stagger_end_tick ≤ T` clears it (the stagger ends on this tick). While `DOWNED`, `T ≥ death_tick` sets `loco_state := DEAD`; the cap was read first in step 1, so a recovery written on this tick wins (D.14), and a `give_up` apply has already lowered `death_tick` in P2.
262	3. **Movement wins over a channel.** `octant := intent_octant`. If `octant ≠ NONE` and `channel_ref` is set, clear `channel_ref`, `channel_face` and `channel_body` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G6; INTERNAL fix)* **now**, so the move takes effect on this same tick and the first movement step is not lost.
263	4. **`loco_state`: one total precedence function**, highest first: `DEAD` (latches until a restore replaces the block) > `DOWNED` (`T_downed` set; also while the body is the pod, D60, so a downed actor in the pod is `DOWNED` and `give_up` is live) > `IN_POD` (the actor's `body_of_actor` is a pod body, a pure Body read) > `STAGGERED` (`stagger_end_tick` set) > `CHANNELLING` (`channel_ref` set) > the locomotion class function of `(octant, run, cap, stowed_heavy, carry_ref)`. **Every non-class exit lands directly on the class member (or the next flag down) on the tick its flag clears — a stagger ending, a `DOWNED` recovery, leaving the pod — with no intermediate `IDLE` tick** (the creative-director's lean: "escape is never blocked" serves Pillar 1, and a one-tick `IDLE` after a lock would be a tick of lost control; it also removes a state the class function would otherwise have to contradict).
264	5. **`v_eff`** from D.4 using the `loco_state` just computed (and the D.5 ladder when its knob is non-zero).
265	6. **Facing** from D.8, top-down, using the same `loco_state` and the stored `channel_face`.
266	7. **Bookkeeping and derived values:** `ramp_ticks`, `walk_ticks`, `last_octant`, `decel_k`, `chest_sim`, `hand_sim`; then the read view is published.

326	*Scope note.* Every formula below is kinematics, quantisation, timing or scoring math for the player's body and hands; nothing here is a balance curve that reads Attention, sanity or rhythm state (PC-10 — a formula whose inputs include any of those is a Pillar 2 violation, not a tuning choice). **Every numeric default is provisional until the motion-integrity spike, the pacing spike and the MVP playtest.** Source column vocabulary follows the kernel GDD: `constant` = compiled, changing it is a code change; `data file` = read at boot from `assets/data/` (speeds, strides, noise, the chest/hand-point tables and every hysteresis live there — a balance pass edits the file, not the code); `calculated` = derived at runtime; `registry` = a locked cross-system fact from `design/registry/entities.yaml`; `Settings` = a player-facing option. All ticks are the kernel's integer `T`; "render s" is wall time measured by the Adapter or Presenter, which the sim never sees (kernel H9). Octant and facing indices use **one table** shared by `set_move_intent.octant`, `controller.state.facing`, the unit-vector table, `CHEST_POINT` and `HAND_POINT`: `0 = E, 1 = NE, 2 = N, 3 = NW, 4 = W, 5 = SW, 6 = S, 7 = SE, 8 = NONE` (counter-clockwise from screen-east with screen `y` down, so angle `θ = atan2(−dy, dx)`); the spawn facing is `S = 6` *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; Section C names the octants but never fixes the index, and three systems must agree on it)*. Where a block has several sub-formulas, the lead-in names the primary one and the rest follow as "Derived:" lines.
327	
328	**D.1 Speed ladder — px/tick, px/s, tiles/s**
329	
330	The `speed_ladder` formula is defined as:
331	
332	`v_px_s = v × TICK_RATE`
333	
334	Derived: `v_tiles_s = v × TICK_RATE / TILE_PX`
335	Derived: `ticks_per_tile = TILE_PX / v`
336	
337	**Variables:**
338	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
339	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
340	| v | int | 1–v_ceil (defaults `v_carry` **1** (registry: `V_CARRY`), `v_walk` **2** (registry: `V_WALK`), `v_run` **3** (registry: `V_RUN`)) | data file (`assets/data/locomotion`) | Whole base px per tick for one gait — integer by PR-4 rule 3 (camera quantum 1) |
341	| TICK_RATE | int | 60 | registry (set-once) | Ticks per simulated second |
342	| TILE_PX | int | 48 | registry (set-once) | Base px per tile |
343	| v_px_s | int | 60–180 (ladder: 60 / 120 / 180 / 240 …) | calculated | The same speed in base px per simulated second |
344	| v_tiles_s | float | 1.25–3.75 | calculated | Tiles per second — the designer-facing pacing figure |
345	| ticks_per_tile | int or float | 16–48 | calculated | Ticks to cross one tile; integer only when `v` divides 48 (1, 2, 3, 4, 6 …) |
346	
347	**Output Range:** The ladder is discrete — at quantum 1 the only speeds that exist are multiples of 60 px/s; there is no 90 or 150 px/s (the pipeline's placeholders were 1.5 / 2.5 px/tick and are superseded). `v_ceil` (D.2) is 3 at the registry defaults, so the usable ladder is {60, 120, 180} px/s = {1.25, 2.5, 3.75} tiles/s; the 13.3-tile default field (640 / 48) crosses in 10.7 / 5.3 / 3.6 s. `ticks_per_tile` is used by the noise-per-tile figure (D.13) and the stride derivation (D.11). Changing `TICK_RATE` changes every px/s figure by `new/old` while the px/tick data stays numerically the same — which is why the data file stores px/tick and the invalidation is listed in Section G.
348	**Example:** `v_walk = 2` → `2 × 60 = 120 px/s`, `120 / 48 = 2.5 tiles/s`, `48 / 2 = 24 ticks per tile`. `v_run = 3` → 180 px/s, 3.75 tiles/s, 16 ticks per tile. `v_carry = 1` → 60 px/s, 1.25 tiles/s, 48 ticks per tile.
349	
350	**D.2 Camera invariants and the integer speed ceiling**
351	
352	The `v_ceil` formula is defined as:
353	
354	`v_ceil = min( ceil(LAG_CUT_eff / (FOLLOW_TAU_eff × TICK_RATE)) − 1 , floor((INNER_BOX_FRAC × field_h − L_MAX_eff) / (FOLLOW_TAU_eff × TICK_RATE)), V_LADDER_MAX )` with `s = field_h / 360`, `L_MAX_eff = LOOKAHEAD_PX × s`, `LAG_CUT_eff = LAG_CUT × s`, `FOLLOW_TAU_eff = FOLLOW_TAU × min(1, s)` (pipeline D.6–D.10; `INNER_BOX_FRAC` = 0.30) *(Amended 2026-10-26 — consistency check: solver length knobs scale by `s = field_h / 360`; re-review, general rule G1: the follow time constant scales by `min(1, s)`, as the pipeline's D.6 has it, not by `s`)*
355	
356	Derived (I1, pipeline D.6 / registry `camera_cut_predicates`): `v_max × TICK_RATE × FOLLOW_TAU < LAG_CUT` — the steady-state follow lag never trips the lag-cut
357	Derived (I2, pipeline D.10 / registry `camera_follow`): `v_max × TICK_RATE × FOLLOW_TAU_eff + L_MAX_eff ≤ INNER_BOX_FRAC × field_h` (with `FOLLOW_TAU_eff = FOLLOW_TAU × min(1, s)`, `L_MAX_eff = LOOKAHEAD_PX × s`, `s = field_h / 360`) — lag plus full look-ahead stays inside the 30 % inner box *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera)*
358	Derived (**I2 in integer form — the one form the pipeline loader asserts; this is invariant 2 itself, and the earlier separate invariant 17 that restated it is deleted** — *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review: merged into I2*): `v_run × TICK_RATE × FOLLOW_TAU_ms + 1000 × LOOKAHEAD_PX ≤ INNER_BOX_PM × 360` with `FOLLOW_TAU_ms = round(1000 × FOLLOW_TAU)` and `INNER_BOX_PM = 300` (per mille of the 360-row field) — i.e. `180·τ + L ≤ 108` at the defaults (`32400 + 72000 = 104400 ≤ 108000`). The registry gives `FOLLOW_TAU` (0–0.20 s) and `LOOKAHEAD_PX` (48–75) independent ranges, which form a box whose corner `(0.20, 75)` breaks the constraint (`36 + 75 = 111 > 108`); the pipeline loader must assert the joint form, not the two ranges, and does it in integers so no float rounding can move the verdict. **Division guard:** at `FOLLOW_TAU = 0` (a legal value, rigid follow) both the I1 term and the I2 term have a zero denominator and are treated as **unbounded** (skipped from the `min`); `v_ceil` is then bounded by the remaining terms and by `V_LADDER_MAX` = 4, and the joint constraint reduces to `1000 × LOOKAHEAD_PX ≤ 300 × field_h`. `v_run` stays a knob whose range depends on the pair `(τ, L)`: `v_run ≤ v_ceil(τ, L)`.
359	
360	**Variables:**
361	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
362	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
363	| v_max | int | = `v_run` (**3**) | data file (derived: the largest gait speed) | Fastest whole-px/tick speed any crewmate body can move; read by the pipeline's G check |
364	| TICK_RATE | int | 60 | registry | — |
365	| FOLLOW_TAU | float | 0–0.20 s (**0.18**) at the 360-row field | registry (pipeline's knob) | Camera follow time constant; steady-state lag = `v_px_s × FOLLOW_TAU` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera)* |
366	| LAG_CUT | int | **48** base px | registry (pipeline's knob) | Follow lag at which the camera cuts instead of panning |
367	| LOOKAHEAD_PX | int | 48–75 (**72**) base px at the default field | registry (pipeline's knob) | Maximum look-ahead offset (`L_MAX` in the pipeline's wording) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera)* |
368	| field_h | int | 216 / 270 / **360** / 720 base px (Deck 400 / 800) | calculated (pipeline: visible field at the current zoom step) | Visible field height; 360 at the default field, 270 zoomed in at k = 4 and 216 at k = 5 (1080p), 720 zoomed out; every length in the I2 term scales by `s = field_h / 360` except the follow time constant, which scales by `min(1, s)`; the term is scale-free for `s ≤ 1` and only loosens for `s > 1` |
369	| v_ceil | int | 0–4 | calculated (build-time check) | The largest integer px/tick satisfying both inequalities |
370	
371	**Output Range:** At the registry defaults I1 gives `v_max × 10.8 < 48` → `v_max < 4.44` (integer 4) and I2 gives `10.8 × v_max + 72 ≤ 108` → `v_max ≤ 3.33` (integer 3); **I2 binds and `v_ceil = 3`** — `v_run = 3` sits exactly on the ceiling (lag 32.4 px; 32.4 + 72 = 104.4 ≤ 108, a 3.6 px margin). Both inequalities are **build invariants** (Section G): a data file with `v_run = 4` fails to load. Sensitivity, computed so the coupled knobs are visible: holding `v_run = 3` and `LOOKAHEAD_PX = 72`, I2 holds only for **`FOLLOW_TAU ≤ 0.20`** (0.21 → 37.8 + 72 = 109.8 > 108); holding `FOLLOW_TAU = 0.18`, **`LOOKAHEAD_PX ≤ 75`** (76 → 108.4 > 108). The registry ranges (FOLLOW_TAU 0–0.20 s, LOOKAHEAD_PX 48–75 at the default field) are the pipeline's own and each is valid only with the other at its default; this GDD does not narrow them but asserts the **joint** constraint above, because their box corner `(0.20, 75)` fails I2 (111 > 108) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; registry request on `speed_ceiling`)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera)* `field_h = 270` (zoom-in at k = 4, `s = 0.75`) gives `floor((81 − 54) / 8.1) = 3` and `field_h = 216` (k = 5, `s = 0.6`) gives `floor((64.8 − 43.2) / 6.48) = 3` — because every length in the I2 term scales by `s` (the follow time constant by `min(1, s)`), **`v_ceil` is exactly 3 at every zoomed-in step (`s ≤ 1`) and at least 3 at every step**: zoomed out the lag does not grow with `s` while the field does, so at `field_h = 720` (`s = 2`, `FOLLOW_TAU_eff` stays 0.18) the I2 term is `floor((216 − 144) / 10.8) = 6`, the I1 term is `ceil(96 / 10.8) − 1 = 8`, and `v_ceil = min(8, 6, V_LADDER_MAX = 4) = 4`; running is never clamped by zoom (decided 2026-10-26, consistency check; Section C row 8; re-review: the earlier "the same integer at every step" was false for `s > 1`, where the old `τ × s` scaling also over-stated the lag as 64.8 px). Scaling `L_MAX` alone would not have sufficed (`32.4 + 54 = 86.4 > 81` at 270 rows). `v_ceil` can be negative in principle (`LOOKAHEAD_PX > 0.30 × field_h`); the build check treats `v_ceil < v_run` as a failure and names the binding inequality.
372	**Example:** `LAG_CUT = 48, FOLLOW_TAU = 0.18, TICK_RATE = 60, LOOKAHEAD_PX = 72, field_h = 360` → I1 term `ceil(48 / 10.8) − 1 = ceil(4.44) − 1 = 4`; I2 term `floor((108 − 72) / 10.8) = floor(3.33) = 3`; `v_ceil = min(4, 3) = 3`. With the pipeline's old `LAG_CUT = 24` (before the 2026-10-26 amendment) I1 would have given `ceil(2.22) − 1 = 2` and running would have been impossible — the reason the amendment mattered to this GDD.
373	
374	**D.3 Fixed-point sub-pixel integration and the diagonal step cadence**
375	
376	The `locomotion_axis_step` formula (Body's `LocomotionStep`, run once per axis per tick, x then y, before that axis's AABB sweep) is defined as:
377	
378	`sub_a += UNIT[octant].a × v_eff;  step_a = trunc(sub_a / 256);  sub_a −= step_a × 256;  moved_a = sweep_a(step_a)` — the axis position advances by `moved_a`
379	
380	Derived (unit table, 1/256 px, screen `y` down): `UNIT = [(256, 0), (181, −181), (0, −256), (−181, −181), (−256, 0), (−181, 181), (0, 256), (181, 181)]` for octants 0–7
381	
382	**Variables:**
383	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
384	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
385	| octant | int | 0–7 (8 = NONE never reaches this step) | calculated (`controller.state.octant`, written by `controller.step`) | Movement direction |
386	| v_eff | int | 0–3 | calculated (D.4) | Effective whole-px/tick speed this tick |
387	| UNIT[o].a | int | {−256, −181, 0, 181, 256} | constant (Body's table; 181 = round(256 / √2)) | Per-axis velocity scale in 1/256 px for octant `o`, axis `a ∈ {x, y}` |
388	| sub_a | int | −255–255 | calculated (`body.state.sub`, persisted; zeroed on stop and on any octant change; preserved across `post_restore`, registry `move_octant_reset`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics)* | Sub-pixel accumulator for axis `a`, 1/256 px |
389	| step_a | int | −3–3 | calculated | Whole px requested on axis `a` this tick (before collision) |
390	| moved_a | int | −3–3, `|moved_a| ≤ |step_a|` | calculated (after the axis sweep) | Whole px actually moved on axis `a` after the 1-px AABB sweep against Layout footprints |
391	
392	**Output Range:** `|step_a| ≤ ceil(256 × 3 / 256) = 3` per tick. `trunc` (round toward zero) rather than `floor` is **mandatory** so that W motion is the exact mirror of E motion: with `floor`, a residual of −181 would yield `step = −1, sub = 75` on the first tick westward while the eastward twin yields `step = 0, sub = 181` — a 1-px asymmetry between the mirrored facings *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; Section C says "1/256-px fixed point" without naming the rounding rule, and the choice is observable)*. The diagonal magnitude is `√(181² + 181²) = 255.97` → 0.012 % short of cardinal — inside PC-3's "0.1 %". Because both diagonal axes carry identical `|sub|` sequences, every diagonal tick moves `(±k, ±k)` — a diagonal is always exactly 45°. `sub_a` **resets to 0 on stop and on any octant change** *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; PC-3 resets on stop only; carrying a signed residual across a reversal — e.g. −106 then eastward +256 → 150 → `step 0` — would produce a one-tick hitch on every direction change, and resetting costs at most 255/256 px per change)*; it is **not** reset on a gait change (walk → run keeps the residual). Over any 256 consecutive ticks in one octant the per-axis displacement is **exactly** `181 × v_eff` px for a diagonal (and `256 × v_eff` px, i.e. `v_eff` per tick, for a cardinal), with `sub` returning to exactly 0 — PC-18 test 2's "362 ± 1" is tightenable to "exactly 362, `sub = 0`" (finding).

The precedence order is normative: carry beats run (no carry-run cycle), cap beats run (walk-only is a shown state), a stowed HEAVY item beats run (the same walk-only shape, `loco_state == WALK`, `PC_RUN_SUPPRESSED{heavy}` counts; the pack's weight is the readable reason and `cue_input_ignored` plays on the press, PC-2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D18)*, and the ramp counts only while the state is RUN, so stop-and-restart restarts the ramp.

430	The `stop_ladder` formula is defined as:
431	
432	`v_eff(T_rel + k) = floor(v_rel × (STOP_DECEL_TICKS − k) / STOP_DECEL_TICKS)  for k = 1 … STOP_DECEL_TICKS, after octant → NONE at tick T_rel, moving in last_octant (overrides D.4's first line for those k ticks)`

438	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|

440	| STOP_DECEL_TICKS | int | **{0}** (the dormant ladder values 2 and 3 are refused at load until Body's interface carries a motion octant, Open Question 29) | data file | Ticks over which speed steps down to 0; 0 = stop on the same tick *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |

453	Derived (keyboard): `s = (right − left, down − up) ∈ {−1, 0, 1}²` — keys override the stick while any move key is held *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; a sum would need a magnitude clamp and a second hysteresis; override is one rule)*

457	Derived: `o_raw = floor((θ + 22.5) / 45) mod 8`
458	Derived: `δ = |wrap180(θ − 45 × o_cur)|`

461	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
462	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
463	| s | vec2 float | [−1, 1]² | calculated (device) | Composed movement vector; keyboard components are exact integers |
464	| m | float | 0–1 (stick); 0, 1 or √2 (keys) | calculated | Deflection magnitude |
465	| MOVE_DEADZONE | float | 0.15–0.35 (**0.25**) | Settings (range from the accessibility-specialist) | Deflection below which the stick reads NONE |
466	| MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT | float | 0–0.10 (**0.05**) | data file | Release band: once moving, the stick must fall below `MOVE_DEADZONE − EXIT` to read NONE *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; without it a stick resting on the 0.25 ring flickers NONE ↔ octant every frame, each flicker an intent and, during a channel, an abort)* |

469	| o_cur | int | 0–8 | calculated (Adapter's last submitted octant) | Current octant |
470	| OCTANT_HYSTERESIS_DEG | float | 3–8 (**5**) | data file | Extra angle past a sector boundary before the octant changes |

474	**Output Range:** Nine values. The stick must swing `22.5 + 5 = 27.5°` from the current sector's centre to leave it, so the dead band between two adjacent octants is 10° wide, centred on the boundary; a stick parked exactly on a boundary holds whichever octant it entered from. The invariant `OCTANT_HYSTERESIS_DEG < 22.5` (Section G) keeps the switch reachable. Keyboard input has no angular hysteresis (digital, exact) and `A + D` composes to `s.x = 0` — opposite keys cancel; all four keys → `(0, 0)` → NONE *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; simplest deterministic rule; "last-pressed wins" is a possible Settings option, not MVP)*. A sweep that crosses two sectors in one frame jumps directly to `o_raw`; the hysteresis only prevents chatter, never slows a turn.

Returning, it must pass `θ = 45 − 27.5 = 17.5°` to go back to E. Stick relaxes to `m = 0.22` while NE: `0.22 ≥ 0.20` → still NE; at `m = 0.19` → NONE. 521	
522	The Controller defines **no look-ahead formula and no look-ahead knob of its own.** User ruling D6 option B (while running, the camera look-ahead is weighted toward the movement direction; camera only, the beam stays honest and the sim is untouched) is implemented once, in the pipeline's D.7 `look_ahead` (registry `camera_lookahead`): `L_target = L_MAX_eff · ((1 − w) · m · û(aim) + w · û_v)` with `w = LOOKAHEAD_RUN_WEIGHT · smoothstep(V_WALK, V_RUN, |v|)`; `LOOKAHEAD_RUN_WEIGHT` (alias `W_RUN`) defaults to **0.50**, safe range 0–0.75, `[PLACEHOLDER]`, and `v` is the avatar's committed displacement per tick (`pos_curr − pos_prev`, the read the follow target already makes). The earlier Controller-side knob `RUN_LOOKAHEAD_MOVE_WEIGHT` (default 0.75, range 0.55–0.90, keyed on `loco_state == RUN`) and its constraints C1–C3 are **withdrawn** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G1)*: the two formulas differed in default, range, key and acceptance numbers (+36 px against 0), the Controller's old C2 (`w > 0.5`) rejected the pipeline's default, and both could not be built. What stays on the Controller's side, and is tested here:
523	
524	- **The weight is keyed on the gait the player chose, never on rhythm.** `w` is a function of the avatar's committed speed only; nothing reads Attention, rhythm, sanity or the beam's lit state, so Pillar 2's design test (the same input gives the same movement and beam motion in both rhythms) is untouched.
525	- **The sim is untouched.** `aim_angle`, the beam's `Light2D` rotation, `facing` and every sim block are bit-identical for any `LOOKAHEAD_RUN_WEIGHT`; only where the picture is centred changes.
526	- **Inner-box safety (C1, kept).** `(1 − w) · m · û(aim) + w · û_v` is a convex combination of vectors of length ≤ 1 for `w` in [0, 1], so `|L_target| ≤ L_MAX_eff` and the inner-box inequality of D.2 (32.4 + 72 = 104.4 ≤ 108) holds unchanged; no new invariant is needed.
527	
528	**Variables:** none are the Controller's; `LOOKAHEAD_RUN_WEIGHT`, `V_WALK`, `V_RUN`, `L_MAX_eff` and the smoothstep belong to the pipeline (D.7, Tuning Knobs, registry). The Controller supplies `pos_prev`, `pos_curr` (through Body) and the raw aim.
529	
530	**Output Range:** `|L_target| ≤ L_MAX_eff` always. At the pipeline's 0.50 and a full run, an aim straight back gives `L_target = 0`: the camera sits on the follow pose instead of leaning 72 px behind, so turning your back on the pursuer costs the view of it by presentation alone (the D6 intent), and the lean never leans *forward* of the avatar for a backwards aim. Entering and leaving a run eases through the pipeline's `L_SLEW_MAX`.
531	**Example** (pipeline numbers, `m = 1`): running E, `û_v = (1, 0)`, `w = 0.50`. Aim E: `L_target` = 72 px ahead. Aim NE (screen y down, `û_aim = (0.707, −0.707)`): `û_look = 0.5 × (0.707, −0.707) + 0.5 × (1, 0) = (0.854, −0.354)`, magnitude 0.924, **66.5 px**. Aim W: `0.5 × (−1, 0) + 0.5 × (1, 0) = (0, 0)`, **0 px**, where the unweighted look-ahead would have put the camera 72 px behind. The same aim W while walking (`w = 0`): 72 px behind.
532	**Hand-off to the pipeline's owner (cross-GDD note, not edited here):** (1) the pipeline keys `w` on `|v|` through `smoothstep(2, 3, |v|)` over integer displacements; a *walking* diagonal step of 2 px per axis has `|v| = 2.83` and gives `r ≈ 0.93`, so a diagonal walk leans toward the movement on those ticks and the cadence (1, 1, 2, 1, 2 …, D.3) makes `w` flicker. A `loco_state == RUN` key (the Controller already publishes `loco_state` in its `SIM` read view) removes both defects and is the review's recommendation; (2) the old Controller bound `w > 0.5` (aim back never leans the camera behind the avatar) sits exactly on the pipeline's default 0.50 and is lost below it, so the pipeline's safe range should start at 0.50 if the D6 intent is to hold.
533	
534	**D.8 Facing from committed aim — sector hysteresis and overrides**
535	
536	The `facing` formula (registry: `facing_from_aim`; `controller.step`, every tick, no easing; rules evaluated top-down, first match wins) is defined as:
537	
538	`facing = facing_prev if loco_state ∈ {STAGGERED, DOWNED, DEAD} (rule 1, frozen);  (channel_face if channel_face ≠ none else facing_prev) if loco_state == CHANNELLING (rule 2: the stored octant written by `set_channel_ref`; `channel_face = none`, the ACTOR_SELF self-patch, holds `facing_prev`, so the body neither turns to the aim nor to a target; rules 3 to 6 never apply while CHANNELLING; the chest lamp still follows aim);  octant if loco_state == RUN (rule 3);  f_aim if aim_live (rule 4);  octant if octant ≠ NONE (rule 5);  facing_prev otherwise (rule 6)` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6/G1, blocker PC-1(b))*
539	
540	Derived: `f_aim_raw = posmod(floor((aim_angle + 256) / 512), 8)` (`posmod`, as every `mod` in D.7 and D.8)
541	Derived: `f_aim = f_aim_raw if cdist(aim_angle, 512 × facing_prev) > 256 + FACING_HYSTERESIS, else facing_prev`
542	Derived: `sheet = facing ∈ {3, 4, 5} ? mirror_of(facing) : facing; flip_h = facing ∈ {3, 4, 5}` (NW→NE, W→E, SW→SE)
543	Derived: `octant_of(r)` for an integer vector `r = anchor_o − foot` (computed by the channel owner at the `begin_*` apply and passed as `face_octant`, PC-1 b): NONE if `r = (0, 0)`; otherwise the octant `o ∈ 0..7` that maximises `dot(UNIT[o], r)` with `UNIT` of D.3 (integers only, no trig), ties to the smaller `o`. Worked: `r = (−40, 30)` gives dot values SW(5) = 181·40 + 181·30 = 12670, W(4) = 10240, S(6) = 7680 → 5 (SW); `r = (60, −10)` gives E(0) = 15360, NE(1) = 10860 + 1810 = 12670 → 0 (E); `r = (181, −75)` gives E = 46336 and NE = 32761 + 13575 = 46336, a tie → 0; `r = (0, 0)` → NONE. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6/G1, blocker PC-1(b))*
544	
545	**Variables:**
546	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
547	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
548	| aim_angle | int | 0–4095 | calculated (`controller.state`, last applied `set_aim`) | Committed aim |
549	| facing_prev | int | 0–7 | calculated (`controller.state.facing` last tick; spawn **6 = S**) | Previous facing |
550	| FACING_HYSTERESIS | int | 32–96 (**64** = 1/64 turn = 5.625°) | data file | Extra distance past a sector boundary (256 units = 22.5°) before facing flips; must be ≥ `AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD` (one send can never straddle it) and < 256 |
551	| aim_live | bool | — | calculated (`controller.state.aim_live`, carried on `set_aim` — D.7) | Mouse: always true; stick: deflected past `AIM_DEADZONE`; keys: an aim key held; `FOLLOW_ALWAYS`: never |
552	| octant | int | 0–8 | calculated | Movement octant |
553	| channel_face | int | 0–7 or none | stored (`controller.state.channel_face`, written by `set_channel_ref`'s `face_octant` = `octant_of(target anchor − foot)` computed by the channel owner at the `begin_*` apply; cleared with `channel_ref`) | The locked work-facing octant; stored data, so a MIRROR client reads it; none for ACTOR_SELF or a zero vector; then rule 2 yields `facing_prev` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6/G1, blocker PC-1(b))* |
554	| facing | int | 0–7 | calculated | Published facing |
555	| flip_h | bool | — | calculated (Presenter) | Mirror flag for the three mirrored facings |
556	
557	**Output Range:** Eight values, every tick, from committed state only. The hysteresis band is 2 × 64 = 128 units = 11.25° wide centred on each boundary; a mouse resting on a boundary never flickers. Facing flips in a single tick (a 180° flick is one tick, D.7's send permitting). The overrides are evaluated top-down and the first match wins, so a runner's facing ignores aim entirely and a stagger freezes whatever was there; a channel whose `channel_face` is none (the ACTOR_SELF self-patch, or a zero vector) holds `facing_prev` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6/G1, blocker PC-1(b))*. `aim_live` must travel with `set_aim` as a boolean payload field *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; PC-4 rules 4–6 branch on it, so it is sim state, and the Adapter is the only thing that knows whether a stick is deflected)*. Co-op: `facing` itself is in `controller.state` and replicates; a MIRROR client never recomputes it from aim, which is why the replicated aim's coarsening bound (≤ `FACING_HYSTERESIS`) is about the *beam* agreeing with the facing, not the facing itself.
558	**Example:** `aim_angle = 764` (67.17°): `f_aim_raw = floor(1020 / 512) = 1 (NE)`; centre of NE is 512, `cdist(764, 512) = 252 ≤ 320` → if `facing_prev = NE` hold NE; if `facing_prev = E (0)`, `cdist(764, 0) = 764 > 320` → NE. Lower half-plane: `aim_angle = 3332` (SE of the avatar, −67.17°) → `f_aim_raw = posmod(floor(3588 / 512), 8) = 7 (SE)`; `aim_angle = 4095` → `floor(4351 / 512) = 8 → posmod 0 (E)`; due south `3072` → `floor(3328 / 512) = 6 (S)`. `aim_angle` is already `posmod`-wrapped by D.7, so `f_aim_raw` is never negative; `cdist` uses `posmod` too *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: 765 → 764 and the wrap examples)*. Mouse drifts to `aim_angle = 800` (70.3°): `cdist(800, 512) = 288 ≤ 320` → NE holds (raw would say N from 768). At 833 (73.2°): `289 → 321 > 320` → N. Running SW while aiming NE → `facing = 5 (SW)`, `sheet = SE`, `flip_h = true`; the beam light still rotates to 67° from the mirrored chest point.
559	
560	**D.9 Reach test and focus score**
561	
562	The `in_reach` formula (sim-side, Interaction's `validate`; integer-only) is defined as:
563	
564	`in_reach(o) = d² ≤ REACH_PX²  ∧  D > 0  ∧  D² × 1000 ≥ COS2_REACH × 65536 × d²  ∧  lit(o)`
565	
566	Derived: `r = anchor_o − foot; d² = r.x² + r.y²; D = dot(UNIT[facing], r)` (integer, 1/256 scale); `COS2_REACH = round(1000 × cos²(REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG)) = 117`
567	Derived (Adapter-side, per render frame, float permitted — it chooses a target, the sim re-checks it): `score(o) = d / REACH_PX + FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT × θ_a / REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG` over candidates with `in_reach(o)`
568	Derived: `focus = argmin score`, kept on the current focus unless `score(best) < score(current) − FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` or the current focus is no longer a candidate; ties → smaller `θ_a`, then smaller entity id
569	Derived: `SELF_FOCUS_SCORE = 2 + FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT × 180 / REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG + FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN`; the self-target (PC-6) is a candidate only when no `in_reach` world candidate exists, and its sticky margin is not applied against a world candidate *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP, blocker PC-6 focus model)*
570	
571	**Variables:**
572	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
573	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
574	| anchor_o | vec2 int | — | calculated (Interaction's per-object interaction anchor; default = footprint centre) | Where the object is "at" for reach |
575	| foot | vec2 int | — | calculated (`body.state.pos_curr`, aliased `pos`; horizontally centred, the foot box's top row) | Foot origin *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics)* |
576	| d | float / d² int | 0–REACH_PX | calculated | Distance to the anchor; the sim compares squares |
577	| REACH_PX | int | 48–96 (**72**) base px | data file | Reach radius — 1.5 tiles; includes the diagonal neighbour at 48√2 = 67.9 |
578	| UNIT[facing] | vec2 int | D.3 table | constant | Facing direction at 1/256 scale (angle `θ_f` is measured from it); the diagonal entries are 255.97/256 of unit length — a 0.02 % bias on the arc edge, accepted |
579	| D | int | — | calculated | `dot(UNIT[facing], r)`; all terms of `in_reach` are integers (64-bit: `D²` ≤ (256 × 96 × 2)² ≈ 2.4 × 10^9, × 1000 fits) |
580	| REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG | float | 45–90 (**70**) | data file | Half-angle of the reach sector about **facing** |
581	| θ_f | float | 0–180° | calculated | Angle between facing and `r` — the arc test |
582	| θ_a | float | 0–180° | calculated (Adapter) | Angle between the **ground-projected aim** and `r` — the score weight. Mouse: the direction from `foot` to `cursor_aim_world` (D.7), so pointing the lamp straight at a floor object scores θ_a ≈ 0 instead of the 30° the chest-height origin would give; stick and keys: the committed `aim_angle` (a direction only). Presentation-side only; `in_reach` and the sim never see it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
583	| lit(o) | bool | — | calculated (Emitter State's exposure query ≥ the technical-artist's threshold) | Object is lit |
584	| FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT | float | 0.5–2.0 (**1.0**) | data file | Weight of aim against proximity |
585	| FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN | float | 0–0.25 (**0.10**) | data file | Score advantage a challenger needs to take focus *(adopted — decision log 2026-10-26; two near-equal candidates would otherwise trade the prompt every frame as the aim jitters within one quantum)* |
586	| in_reach | bool | — | calculated | Candidate predicate; also the sim's validation of the Adapter's chosen target |
587	| score | float | 0–≈ 2.4 at defaults while facing tracks aim; ≤ 3.57 in every state (RUN) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP, blocker PC-6 focus model)* | calculated | Lower is better |
588	| SELF_FOCUS_SCORE | float | load-computed: 2 + 2.5714 + 0.10 = 4.6714 at defaults; 2 + 2.0 × 180 / 45 + 0.25 = 10.25 at the knob extremes W = 2.0, H = 45°, M = 0.25 | calculated at load (not a knob) | Score of the PC-6 self-target; above every world score in every state (invariant 19) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP, blocker PC-6 focus model)* |
589	
590	**Output Range:** `in_reach` is exact integer arithmetic (sim-safe, G3-pure): `d² ≤ 5184`; `D > 0` excludes everything at or behind 90°, and the squared-cosine test (cos² 70° = 0.117, multiplied through by 256² = 65536 so no division occurs) the rest of the arc — objects behind the player are never candidates. `score` is bounded by `d / 72 ≤ 1` plus `W × θ_a / 70`; because aim and facing can differ by up to 22.5° + 5.6° (D.8) while the arc extends 70° from facing, `θ_a` can reach ≈ 98° and the score ≈ 2.4 while facing tracks aim (up to 22.5° + 5.6° = 28.1° apart); under RUN (D.8 rule 3, facing = movement octant whatever the aim) `θ_a` can reach 180°, so the all-state bound is `1 + FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT × 180 / REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG` = 1 + 2.5714 = 3.57 at defaults and 1 + 8 = 9.0 at W = 2.0, H = 45° *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP, blocker PC-6 focus model)* — it is a ranking, not a probability, and is never clamped. Minimum 0: an object at the foot on the aim line. The sim never computes `score`; it only validates the Adapter's chosen target with `in_reach`, so the float is presentation-only and cannot desync. The mouse has no pick-under-cursor path: moving the cursor moves the aim, and the aim weights the score.
591	**Example:** Facing E, aim at 10° above east. Hatch A at `r = (60, −10)`: `d = 60.8`, `θ_f = 9.5°`, `θ_a = 0.5°` → candidate; `score = 0.845 + 0.007 = 0.85`. Crate C at `r = (−20, 40)`: `D = −20 × 256 < 0` → never a candidate. If the aim swings down to −40° (toward B): B's `θ_a = 5°` → `0.59 + 0.07 = 0.66`; A's `θ_a = 49.5°` → `0.845 + 0.71 = 1.55`; B's advantage `0.89 > 0.10` → focus switches to B.

593	**D.10 Hold-to-confirm bar and tap-to-confirm**
594	
595	The `confirm_bar` formula (Adapter-local, render time) is defined as:
596

649	**Output Range:** `odometer` is 64-bit: at 768 units/tick (run) it reaches 2^63 after ≈ 1.9 × 10^14 s — overflow is impossible and unhandled beyond a width assertion (kernel D.14 pattern). With `STRIDE = v × TICK_RATE / ANIM_FPS = 5v` the moving cycle runs at **exactly 12 fps on every gait and in every octant**: cardinal walk adds 512/tick → a frame every 5 ticks; diagonal walk adds `(k + k) × 181` per tick, averaging 511.9/tick (28 units short per 256 ticks — one dropped frame (2560 units) every ≈ 23,400 ticks ≈ 6.5 min of continuous diagonal walking, invisible). Sliding along a wall on a diagonal (one axis blocked) animates at **0.50** of the cardinal pace (`ODO_W` 181 per pixel on one axis: 1.414 px/tick × 181 = 256 units against 512 for a cardinal), while the body itself slides at 0.707 of its speed, so the cycle runs slower than the feet's ground speed during a slide *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier text claimed 0.707 here and in Edge Cases and an acceptance criterion, while another criterion fixed the weight at 181, which gives 0.50; the two contradicted each other)*. The rule is **Ship Body's (BDY-19, `ODO_W[move octant]`)** and this GDD does not contradict it: it documents the 0.50 consequence. If the playtest finds the slide cycle too slow, the alternative that restores 0.707 is to weight by the axes that actually moved (256 per pixel for a single-axis move, 181 per pixel for a two-axis move); that is Body's change, recorded as Open Question 22. Walking into a wall adds 0 and the cycle freezes on its current frame (PC-18 test 8). `frame_moving` is continuous across octant changes, facing changes, gait changes (the stride divisor changes but `cycle_pos_prev` is re-based on the same tick, so no jump) and the forward/reverse switch. One-shot states clamp on the last frame: the 4-frame stagger finishes at tick 20 and holds for the remaining `STAGGER_TICKS − 20`; the 6-frame down finishes at tick 30 — so **`STAGGER_TICKS ≥ 20` is a floor** (the quantities block's 18 would truncate the sheet; Section G corrects the range to 20–45). Remote bodies use the same formulas from MIRROR state; `anim_counter` is per-Presenter and may differ between clients by a whole cycle without any pillar consequence (phase, not pose, is unreplicated).
650	**Example:** Walking east, `odometer` goes 0, 512, 1024 … → `cycle_pos` 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1 (tick 5) … → frame 1 at tick 5, frame 2 at tick 10, wraps at tick 40: 12 fps. Back-pedal: walking W while facing E (`dot < 0`) with `anim_counter = 5` → frames 5, 4, 3 … ; the player turns to face W mid-stride (`dot > 0` now) at `anim_counter = 3` → frames 3, 4, 5 …; nothing jumps. Stagger entered at T = 5000: frames 0, 1, 2, 3 at T = 5000, 5005, 5010, 5015; frame 3 held through T = 5029; IDLE at T = 5030.

734	**D.15 Input-to-first-pixel latency**
735	
736	The `L_pixel` formula (this GDD's instance of kernel D.4, with the Adapter's sampling point fixed) is defined as:
737	
738	`L_pixel = L_sample + L_tick + L_interp + L_render`
739	
740	Derived: `L_sample ∈ [0, frame_duration)` — age of the device event at the physics-callback sample
741	Derived: `L_tick ≈ 0` wall — sample → `Kernel.step()` is the same call; one tick of *simulated* latency by construction (P1 freeze → P2 apply → P3 integrate)
742	Derived: `L_render ∈ [0, frame_duration]` — P5 notify → the frame that draws it
743	Derived *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `L_interp = tick_duration / step_px` — the Presenter draws `floor(lerp(pos_prev, pos_curr, tick_alpha))`, so a tick's motion is spread over the following render interval and the first whole pixel appears only when `tick_alpha × step_px ≥ 1`, i.e. after `1 / step_px` of a tick (8.3 ms at the 2 px walk step, 5.6 ms at the 3 px run step, up to 16.7 ms at a 1 px step); a sub-pixel position is never drawn (PR-4), so the earlier "first visible sub-step that frame" does not exist

747	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|

749	| L_sample | float | 0–16.7 ms | calculated | Wall age of the newest input event when the Adapter samples immediately before `Kernel.step()` |
750	| L_tick | float | ≈ 0 ms wall (exactly 1 simulated tick) | calculated | Sample-to-commit within one `Kernel.step()` call |
751	| L_render | float | 0–16.7 ms | calculated | Same-frame draw if the physics callback precedes `_process` (ADR to verify); next frame otherwise |
752	| L_interp *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | float | 5.6–16.7 ms | calculated | Delay from the tick's commit to the first whole-pixel step of the lerp-then-floor draw: `tick_duration / step_px` |
753	| L_pixel | float | ≈ 6–42 ms at the 2 px walk step (≈ 6–39 at the 3 px run step, 6–50 at a 1 px step; + display scan-out) | calculated | Press → the body's first moved pixel |
754	| L_ack | float | ≤ frame_duration | calculated | Press → pre-play (sound, hand animation, bar): 0 ticks by construction |
755	
756	**Output Range:** Best case a few ms plus `L_interp` (event arrives just before the sample, tick runs, same frame draws, first pixel after `L_interp`); worst ≈ 33 ms + `L_interp` at 60 fps, i.e. ≈ 42 ms for the 2 px walk step (event just after a sample waits a frame, then draws next frame, then waits for the first whole pixel) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; the sim contribution is exactly one tick and never two, because the sample precedes P0 of the tick it lands in (submit before `step()` → `queued_tick = T − 1`, in tick T's batch). findings.section: PC-7, PC-2, Interactions rows 5 and 1, Edge Cases L826, Tuning LIT_ABORT_GRACE_TICKS, OQ 25, OQ 30(b), AC-PCI-022, AC-PCI-114 (carried over, G3)
findings.finding: Interaction OQ 47 is resolved against the Controller, and the Controller still builds on the declined asks. The reason stays `BUSY` and a separate `MOVING` is declined. `LIT_ABORT_GRACE_TICKS` is not adopted at MVP: default 0, routed to accessibility. Interaction L182 lists moving under BUSY. The Controller still says 'MOVING' and 'proposed grace 30' at PC-7 L182, the PC-2 'MOVING tell' wording, Tuning L974 (default 30) and OQ 25. OQ 30(b)'s 'done 2026-10-28' clause still lists 'the reject reason MOVING; LIT_ABORT_GRACE_TICKS', which is a false done claim. AC-PCI-022 asserts `Rejected(MOVING)` and cannot pass a stub that conforms to Interaction. AC-PCI-114's 30-tick branch has no owner.
