Correct OQ 25 and OQ 30(b), and grep 'MOVING' and 'proposed' afterwards (G3).

findings.section: D.14 examples (L731-732) and AC-PCI-144, against suit-and-equipment SE-1 (new, from the sibling pass)
findings.finding: Suit's cross-GDD pass moved `suit.vitals` to divisor 6, offset 2 (SE-1 L153, registration (6, 2)), so Suit writes on ticks with T mod 6 == 2. The Controller's D.14 first example, its second example, AC-PCI-144 and the Edge Case on recovery all say 'Suit ticks are multiples of 6' and use 10,002, 10,152 and 11,796. 10,152 mod 6 is 0, so a Suit stub conforming to its owner cannot write on those ticks. The second example also says the controller reads Suit's value one tick later (11,797), which contradicts PC-15 (`after: suit.vitals`, same tick).
findings.fix: Recompute per G4 on T mod 6 == 2: for example downed at 10,004, press edge 10,106, fill at 10,154, cap written at 10,154; second example Suit write at 11,798, read in the same tick. Remove the one-tick read lag and re-check the '0 to 5 tick' staleness sentence.

findings.section: PC-5 L170, D.7b (L522, L532), Tuning LOOKAHEAD_RUN_WEIGHT row, OQ 28(i), OQ 30(a), AC-PCI-092 (carried over)
findings.finding: The registry `camera_lookahead` and the pipeline's D.7 now key the run weight as `w = LOOKAHEAD_RUN_WEIGHT * r`, with r = 1 iff the committed loco_state == RUN and the avatar moved on any of the last 3 ticks. The Controller still quotes `smoothstep(V_WALK, V_RUN, |v|)` in four places. It also still asks the pipeline owner for the `loco_state == RUN` key, which has already been done, in D.7b hand-off (1), OQ 28(i) and OQ 30(a). AC-PCI-092's stub ('3 px per tick') is keyed on speed.
findings.fix: Replace every quotation of the formula with the registry form. Delete the hand-off asks or mark them done. Key the AC-PCI-092 stub on `loco_state == RUN` and moved-in-3-ticks, and check the walking-diagonal case (|v| = 2.83, w = 0).

findings.section: OQ 24 / Edge Cases L839 / AC-PCI-116 (dark port, carried over; R21)
findings.finding: Still open at 'Next consistency pass', owned by Interaction and Suit. Grep of interaction-system.md and suit-and-equipment.md finds no decision. A home-ship port with an empty cell, no glowstick and no other light answers NOT_LIT forever. R21 does not allow a design call to stay open.
findings.fix: Decide by the least-new-content rule, which keeps the 'go dark' lever from user ruling X5: record dark-lamp death as a deliberate horror outcome. Add a Boarding/Derelict authoring note that is a recommendation, not a requirement, for a self-lit port fixture on the home ship. Mark OQ 24 'Resolved 2026-10-28 delegated ruling R21' and keep AC-PCI-116.

findings.section: AC-PCI-002 L1076 and AC-PCI-210 L1324 / Upstream Suit row L881 (new, from the PC-6 self-target edit)
findings.finding: AC-PCI-002's Adapter read-view allow-list omits Suit's `tool_in_hand(player_id)`, which the PC-6 self-target needs, so the lint fails against a rule it must permit. AC-PCI-210 and the Upstream Suit row say the only Suit read is `locomotion_cap`, but the controller.step class function also reads `stowed_heavy`.
findings.fix: Add `tool_in_hand` and `stowed_heavy` to the AC-PCI-002 allow-list. Reword AC-PCI-210 to 'the Controller Sim reads only `locomotion_cap` and `stowed_heavy`, never the vitals ladder'.

findings.section: PC-8 salvage_carry / registry HOME_BODY (new, from the R5 GAP fix)
findings.finding: `salvage_carry := body_of_actor(actor) != HOME_BODY` has no producer. The registry source is the Controller GDD itself, and its own note says Ship Body's text defines `body_of_actor` but not 'home body'. The cited 'Layout E-44' (PC-8, registry description, Attention AT-3) could not be located in ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md. Without a Body read, the pickup-tick stamp cannot be built.
findings.fix: Have Ship Body (or Layout) publish a pure `home_body_id()` / `is_home_body(body_id)` read, including that a welded derelict is part of the home body, and move the registry `source:` there. Fix the E-44 citation or drop it. Add a unit AC for the weld case: a salvage item picked up in a derelict that is then welded to home stops pushing BURDEN.

findings.section: D.4 walk_ticks / ramp_ticks, PC-17 field table, AC-PCI-193 (carried over)
findings.finding: `walk_ticks` is still 'unbounded' in D.4 and persisted. The snapshot writes 0 while the uninterrupted control keeps counting. If `state_hash(PERSIST)` covers the live block, replay and control diverge and AC-PCI-193 cannot pass. The GDD does not say whether the hash is over live fields or snapshot bytes.
findings.fix: Saturate `walk_ticks` at `WALK_START_TICKS` (identically 0 at the default) and `ramp_ticks` at `RUN_RAMP_TICKS`. Alternatively state that the hash is over canonical snapshot bytes. Add a golden to AC-PCI-193.

findings.section: AC-PCI-157, AC-PCI-175, cursor-warp coordinate space (carried over; R12, R4)
findings.finding: AC-PCI-157 ('median <= 42 ms, 90th percentile <= 50 ms') names no machine and assumes a 60 fps capture, so it cannot hold at the Deck's 30 fps. The Performance block names RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK but this AC does not use them. AC-PCI-175 still says 'C11 yields a world point', but mouse aim uses `cursor_aim_world` (D.14b) and C11 is for prompts only. There is still no in-engine AC for the `warp_mouse` coordinate space; docs/engine-reference does not settle it, so [UNV] is right.
findings.fix: Gate AC-PCI-157 on RM-DESKTOP at 60 fps (42 ms / 50 ms) and give the RM-DECK figure from D.15 at 30 fps (frame 33.3 ms, so the bounds are about 75 ms and 90 ms). Change AC-PCI-175 to cite `cursor_aim_world`. Add an in-engine check: warp the hidden cursor to a known picture offset, read it back, and require the same `aim_q` within ±1.

findings.section: PC-5 mouse-aim trade-off (carried over; not applied this pass)
findings.finding: The recorded trade-off stands unchanged: while running, a still mouse turns the beam by up to atan(36/60), about 31°, as the follow pose trails the avatar (PC-5, D.7, AC-PCI-059). The earlier review and the creative-director rated it the top Pillar 1 feel risk. The GDD now documents it and gates it on the target-acquisition spike (median <= 15°) with ordered fallbacks and R18. The arithmetic checks out (AC-PCI-056: aim_q 764 and 1637 recomputed).
findings.fix: No GDD change is needed before the spike. Keep AC-PCI-061 as the gate, and add the sawing metric (aim_q change across consecutive frames at 144 fps while running with a still cursor) to the spike evidence file.

findings.section: Stale-text sweep, not applied (carried over; G3)
findings.finding: Still present: 'Sixteen systems' (L18; the Downstream table lists about 20); duplicate specialist preamble (L56 and L58); `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` shown as '(0.6–1.2)' in PC-6 L180 against 0.6–1.9 in D.10 and Tuning; 'three HUD and settings surfaces' (L1037, four items); `PC_RUN_SUPPRESSED{carry|cap|channel}` (L795) lacks `heavy`, which D.4 and AC-PCI-147 use; the unreachable 'RUN, cap -> WALK_ONLY, WALK next tick' row (L279, because the stagger fires first); 'provisional' status on designed siblings (Interactions rows 4, 5, 7, 9, 13, 17); Settings, Co-op and Accessibility rows lack the R9 label 'undesigned — provisional contract'; roughly 20 'Section B/C/D/E/G/H' letter references; AC numbering interleaved (223-225 sit among 151-152, 226-230 among 190); header `Last Updated` 2026-10-27 and `Last Verified` 2026-10-26 against amendments dated 2026-10-28; `AIM_ORIGIN_Y` is not a registry entry (the registry mentions it only descriptively at L7108); the `correlation` counter start and wrap are not stated.
findings.fix: One mechanical pass. Grep for each old string afterwards and confirm none remains. Register `AIM_ORIGIN_Y` with source = this GDD. State `correlation` as a u32 starting at 1 per Adapter and wrapping at 2^32 - 1 with token-map eviction. Update the header dates.

findings.section: FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT Tuning row
findings.finding: The row says 'Score max ≈ 1 + 1.4 × this'. D.9 gives the all-state bound as 1 + W × 180 / H = 3.57 at defaults (RUN, where facing ignores aim), and 1.4 holds only while facing tracks aim. The row contradicts D.9 and invariant 19's premise.
findings.fix: Change it to 'while facing tracks aim 1 + 1.4 × W; in every state (RUN) 1 + W × 180 / H', citing D.9.

findings.section: AC-PCI-055, AC-PCI-165, AC-PCI-182 (untestable as written)
findings.finding: AC-PCI-055: 'three distinct footstep cues are audible (the run louder by at least the delta the audio-director specifies in AA-31 — no dB figure is invented here)'. This has no pass line. AC-PCI-165: 'the spike reports whether the 29 % zero-motion ticks read as a visible staircase'. This has no pass line either. AC-PCI-182: 'the bracket shows then hides', with no timing or measure.
findings.fix: AC-055: split into (auto) three distinct cue ids with a 20-tick footfall cadence at every gait, and (manual) loudness, marked 'not assessed until the AA-31 threshold is supplied'. AC-165: 'at 144 Hz, >= 80 % of >= 8 testers report no visible staircase on the carry diagonal; else spike-gated fallback'. AC-182: 'the bracket is visible within 1 frame of a NAV or d-pad edge and hidden within 1 frame of >= 1 px of mouse motion; frame-diff captured and retained'.

findings.section: AC-PCI-105d lint scope vs modular-ship-assembly.md L155 (new, sibling wording)
findings.finding: The lint forbids any clause naming a Class B mutator that says 'proposed'. Assembly L155 reads 'Interaction's proposed Class B `open_channel(...)` and the Controller's `set_channel_ref(...)`' in one sentence. `open_channel` is active in the registry and IA-35 names it. A text lint can false-positive on it, and the word is stale.
findings.fix: In Assembly L155, change 'proposed' to 'published (IA-35)'. Make AC-PCI-105d match per clause that names a mutator, and exclude `open_channel`.

findings.section: D.13 BURDEN gate vs Attention AT-3
findings.finding: The Controller gates BURDEN on loco_state not in {IN_POD, DOWNED, DEAD}. Attention AT-3 excludes IN_POD only. This is moot in practice, because a carry is dropped on DOWNED except in the pod, but two GDDs state two gates.
findings.fix: State one gate. Either cite Attention's, or add to AT-3 that a DOWNED or DEAD holder pushes nothing.

findings.section: PC-9 L186 vs Edge Cases L847 / AC-PCI-199 (DEAD behaviour)
findings.finding: PC-9 says commands are 'validated normally and rejected BUSY where Interaction says so' and that nothing is 'ever Rejected for state'. L847 and AC-PCI-199 say a DEAD seat 'accepts no command'. The result a DEAD-state command returns is unstated, so the AC has no pass line.
findings.fix: State: in DEAD every PLAYER command is Rejected(BUSY) (Interaction's immediate class), and rewrite AC-PCI-199 to assert that code.

findings.section: Scope, structure and readability
findings.finding: The document is 505 KB, with preambles and 'Amended' tags nested up to four deep in single paragraphs (PC-6, PC-1 b, D.10). The numbered content and the ACs are consistent. D.1-D.16 arithmetic recomputed correctly: octant_of worked examples, D.2 at s = 0.6/0.75/2, D.10 per-verb caps and frame counts, D.13 noise per tile 24/64/48 and burden 42,000/48,000, AC-PCI-056/095/096. The self-target prompt will show whenever a welder is in hand and no lit object is in reach, which is a deliberate HUD cost recorded in PC-6.
findings.fix: Optional: after the sweep, strip superseded 'Amended' provenance into the review log, and keep a one-page implementation digest per PC rule.
